title: Medication errors after product substitution in three drug shortages at a teaching hospital: a retrospective review
abstract: Objective: to estimate substitution-related medication error rates per 1,000 doses dispensed in three shortage episodes, with pre-episode baselines for the original products. Design: retrospective review of incident reports and the pharmacy intervention log. Results will be reported if research use of incident reports is approved.
introduction: Shortages force substitutions that change concentrations, vial sizes and preparation steps. Local error rates during substitutions are rarely measured, and incident reports are not flagged as shortage-related.
methods: Incident reports are searched with pre-specified product and concentration terms and matched to episode dates; the pharmacy intervention log is reviewed for the same products. A written definition of a substitution-related error is fixed before extraction, and a second pharmacist classifies a random 20 percent. Rates use doses dispensed as the denominator and are compared with the three months before each episode.
results: No data have been extracted; the privacy decision is pending.
discussion: No external evidence was retrieved in two recorded searches, so the discussion will describe local rates without comparison with other hospitals. It will focus on where in the medication process errors arose and what the next substitution plan should change.
limitations: Under-reporting in incident reports; one hospital; small numbers per episode.
conclusion: To be written. Results will be reported by episode, never by staff member or ward.
reportingChecklist: RECORD (STROBE extension for routinely collected data)
